parts.what_was_built: No excavated layout has been published. The site consists of two mounds; the Department of Archaeology and Museums lists Mound A as '503m x533m x 9m' and Mound B as '991m x823m x 9m' and states that 'Both mounds are culturally associated with Mature Harappan phase', citing Mughal's 1974-77 Cholistan survey (doam_ganweriwala). The only published sections we know of are the cuts made by a four-metre-wide road driven through the middle of the site, which Masih (2018: 381, as quoted on harappa.com) says 'did provide ready-made sections across the upper portions of the mounds'; we did not see that chapter. A team led by M. R. Mughal resumed excavation in March 2024 (pakobserver2024; harappacom_origins), but we found no published report of its trenches, walls or dates.
parts.excavator_basis: No excavator's date exists for any wall or street at the site. The Mature Harappan attribution rests on surface finds from Mughal's 1974-77 survey: a 2024 press report quotes Saleem ul Haq that 'The surface finds from Ganweriwala in 1975 showed it was a mature Harappan site and we cannot rule out possibility of finding remains of early period in case of deeper excavation' (pakobserver2024).

syntheses.statement: The government site record gives 'Relative Chronology: 3500 BCE - 1800 BCE' and 'Period: Proto Historic', and describes both mounds as Mature Harappan; its reference is Mughal, 'Ancient Sites in Cholistan, Bahawalpur (1974-77 Survey)', Lahore Museum Bulletin IV(2), July-December 1991. The basis of the 3500 BCE figure is not stated.

Press report: excavations 'resumed in March 2024 after a gap of four decades since its discovery'; the site is 'believed to be the third largest of Indus Valley Civilization between Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro, belonging to an era of 2600 BC'.

Summarising Masih (2018), 'Ganweriwala - A New Perspective', in Walking with the Unicorn, the post reports that Mughal estimated the site at over 80 hectares and a survey ten years later at about half that size, and itself remarks that nothing will be known 'until it is properly excavated and some real trenches are dug deeply into the two known mounds'.

parts.conflicts: The government record gives a relative chronology beginning in 3500 BCE while describing both mounds as Mature Harappan; the press report gives 'an era of 2600 BC'. Neither states a basis, and neither concerns the building of walls or streets.

first_occupation.basis: Unknown. Surface collections are Mature Harappan (doam_ganweriwala; pakobserver2024), and earlier deposits at depth are thought possible but untested (pakobserver2024). The government record's 'Relative Chronology: 3500 BCE - 1800 BCE' is given without a basis.

notes:
Ganweriwala, in the Cholistan desert of Bahawalpur District on the dry Hakra bed, was found by M. R. Mughal in his 1974-77 survey and has not had a published excavation, so we can record neither a layout phase nor a dated wall. What is published is a surface attribution to the Mature Harappan, a government record with an unexplained relative chronology of 3500-1800 BCE, and press notice that Mughal's team resumed excavation in March 2024. The Masih page reference (p. 381) is as quoted on harappa.com; the chapter's range 377-383 comes from the table of contents of Walking with the Unicorn held in research/literature/sources/frenez_2018_identity.txt (p. 377 start; the next chapter begins on p. 384).

Sought and not obtained: Mughal 1997, Ancient Cholistan: Archaeology and Architecture (no full text online); Mughal 1991, Lahore Museum Bulletin IV(2) (not found online); Masih 2018 (Archaeopress offers only a sample PDF); any report of the 2024 excavation. None of the Radiocarbon-journal date lists we were given (TF, PRL, PRLC, BS, Penn) contains a Ganweriwala determination; PRL-III's 'Ganwaria' is a Painted Grey Ware site in Basti district, India. Orientation statements, if any, were not recorded.
